text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: multiple serve-runtime pods in cluster-us-west-2 are being OOM-killed and subsequently evicted due to ephemeral storage pressure on worker nodes. Pager sent to oncall.

alex (oncall): I'm on it. seeing a flurry of OOMKilled + Evicted events for pods: model-cache-*, serve-runtime-*. Node disk usage at ~97%.

sara_infra: Noted. Looks like model cache growth + verbose runtime logs filled /var/lib/kubelet/pods/*/volumes/ on a subset of nodes. Autoscaler couldn't spin up new nodes because node provisioning images hit tmpfs quotas.

priya_se: Any customer impact yet?

emily_support: We have a handful of 503 reports from a single customer org in us-west-2, approx 0.8% of requests in the last 5m. Correlating with pod restarts.

alex (oncall): Plan: 1) Identify most impacted nodes 2) cordon + drain nodes with highest ephemeral usage 3) delete offending model-cache pods so they restart with smaller cache config 4) short-term log truncation to free space 5) scale down non-critical jobs. Doing step 1 now.

mike_eng_runtime: Suggest patching model-cache memory/disk limit not possible live on all pods. Quick workaround: restart model-cache with env RESTART_CACHE=false? Better: remove large cached shards from disk via exec and trigger lazy-repopulate.

sara_infra: Nodes with highest usage: ip-10-0-5-12 (98%), ip-10-0-6-33 (96%), ip-10-0-7-21 (95%). I'm cordoning 10-0-5-12 now.

sara_infra: Command I ran:```\nkubectl cordon ip-10-0-5-12\nkubectl drain ip-10-0-5-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force\n```

alex (oncall): Deleting model-cache pods on that node to free disk. Command:```\nkubectl get pods -o wide -n serving | grep model-cache | grep ip-10-0-5-12 | awk '{print $1}' | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl delete pod {} -n serving\n```

priya_se: Truncating rotated logs on drained node to reclaim ~10-20GB:```\nssh ubuntu@ip-10-0-5-12 'sudo find /var/log/redwood -type f -name "*.log" -exec truncate -s 0 {} +' \n```

emily_support: Customer impact: partial 503s while pods restart. CS notified and sending status update: "We are aware of intermittent 503s in us-west-2 and actively mitigating; ETA ~15-30m."

mike_eng_runtime: On runtime side: lowering model_cache.disk_limit to 20GB on a subset and rolling. Patch command we used in k8s rollout:```\nkubectl set env deployment/model-cache -n serving MODEL_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=21474836480\nkubectl rollout restart deployment/model-cache -n serving --timeout=60s\n```

alex (oncall): After cordon+drain+deletes, node free space rose to 60% on ip-10-0-5-12. Evictions stopped for that node. Proceeding to cordon ip-10-0-6-33 next.

sara_infra: Also disabled debug-level logs for serve-runtime to reduce churn:```\nkubectl patch deployment serve-runtime -n serving --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"serve-runtime","env":[{"name":"LOG_LEVEL","value":"info"}]}]}}}}'\n```

priya_se: Any long-term followups? We should track model cache growth pattern and add eviction thresholds that prefer killing batch-jobs before serve pods.

mike_eng_runtime: Agreed. Postmortem items: - implement cache shard GC when disk > 75% - add node-level tmpfs quotas to avoid provisioning failure - improve autoscaler to consider ephemeral usage.

emily_support: CS: sent follow-up to affected customer with root-cause summary and mitigation steps. Will update once postmortem available.

alex (oncall): Oncall handoff: @sara_infra will take lead for the next 2 hours to complete cordon/drain across remaining nodes; @mike_eng_runtime owns the rollout to apply disk limits and GC. Priya will draft the customer impact note. I'm unassigning pager in 10m.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged. Severity: SEV3 -> SEV2 (customer impact verified). Paging paused.

sara_infra: All targeted nodes cordoned/drained, freed space across 4 nodes. Eviction rate dropped to near zero, serve-runtime error rate trending back to baseline.

alex (oncall): Closing active mitigation tickets, leaving this thread open for postmortem notes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

priya_se: Filed follow-up ticket INFRA-4732: "Model cache disk growth -> eviction cascade" with action items and owners.

mike_eng_runtime: Will schedule a dedicated runbook to handle ephemeral storage pressure and a test to simulate heavy cache growth in staging.

emily_support: Notifying customers that service restored and providing incident reference.

incident-bot: Incident resolved. Total duration ~52m.
